messages:
Ethan (CEO): thanks for coming to the all-hands — opening a short follow-up thread for quick strategy Qs about mission, positioning, market focus, and rivals. i'll be here for ~30 mins. keep Qs punchy.
Jo (Growth): quick one: for GTM, should we lean into "cost" messaging or "reliability / SLAs" more for mid-market buyers?
Sam (Strategy): short answer: reliability first for mid-market, cost becomes strong play for scale-ups that care about unit economics. lead with reliability + predictable ops, then layer cost wins.
Nora (Head of Product): also call out the multi-deployment promise up-front — "hosted -> dedicated -> private" is a buying path.
Riley (Eng): on competitors — how blunt should we be comparing to ModelHouse and BigCloud?
Ethan (CEO): be factual. compare feature gaps: e.g., ModelHouse bundles models but lacks rollout/obs primitives; BigCloud offers endpoints but not dedicated batching optimizations. avoid naming legal issues in public decks; internal sales can be direct.
Jo (Growth): any short reframing for the mission statement for customer-facing copy? current one feels slightly technical.
Sam (Strategy): try this: "Redwood Inference helps engineering teams run LLMs in production with predictable latency, cost, and compliance across any infrastructure." actionable + customer-first.
Nora (Head of Product): roadmap alignment q: should Optimize (cost/perf toolkit) be bumped up over Console improvements? customers often ask for tuning help.
Ethan (CEO): short: yes, prioritize Optimize features that unlock measurable cost reductions (batching suggestions, quant profiles). Console improvements are next, but both continue.
Riley (Eng): specifics: do we commit to SDK parity across hosted and private on day one?
Nora (Head of Product): must have core API parity. SDK niceties can roll out after GA, but customers should be able to switch deployment modes without code changes.
Jo (Growth): what are the top 3 battle-tested objections sales should be ready for?
Sam (Strategy): 1) "We already run on BigCloud" -> answer: predictability + ops reduce build/maintain costs. 2) "We own our models" -> answer: we support customer models and private deployments. 3) "Too expensive" -> answer: show Dedicated economics + Optimize wins.
Ethan (CEO): add: include a customer story in the pitch where fallback routing prevented an outage. specifics sell better than claims.
Riley (Eng): technical competitive q: do we publicly commit to supporting emerging quant libs or wait until stabilization?
Nora (Head of Product): follow major formats quickly but gate support with perf benchmarks. publish compatibility/status in docs.
Jo (Growth): any positioning tweak vs infra vendors who sell self-hosted runtimes?
Sam (Strategy): emphasize managed operational layer + SLOs. Not just runtime: continuous batching, KV cache, rollout policies, tracing, and token-level cost visibility.
Ethan (CEO): KPI note: measure success by reduced avg token latency, % of requests served by cached prefixes, and customer MRR growth from Dedicated deals. More numbers > vague claims.
NotifyBot: all-hands-notes posted to drive at 1765909900 by NotifyBot
Jo (Growth): love the KPI framing. can you share the phrasing we should use in the one-pager?
Sam (Strategy): one-liner for one-pager: "Run LLMs in production with predictable latency, lower unit costs, and enterprise-grade controls — across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments."
Ethan (CEO): i'll drop the one-liner + sam's mission phrasing into the marketing channel and link the updated battlecard for sales. thanks team. if you want deeper competitive decks, ping sam/nora to book time.
Riley (Eng): logging this thread into product-sync for follow-up.
Jo (Growth): thanks ethan 609 :thumbsup:
